explain.say: Here is a puzzle: a computer only understands numbers, yet you can type your name. How? Let us follow one letter, capital A, from your finger to the screen. Look at the first box: you press the A key.

explain.say: Now see the second box. Every computer shares a big code table, like a secret decoder ring. In it, capital A is the number 65, B is 66 and C is 67. Small a is a different number, 97. What do you think D is?

explain.say: See the last box? To show the letter, the computer looks up 65 in the table again and draws the shape of an A. The first table was called ASCII, which is short for a long American name, and it had only 128 characters. Could 128 be enough for every language?

explain.say: Brilliant! The answer was no, so today we use Unicode, a giant table with more than 149 thousand characters: Hindi, Chinese, Arabic, Amharic and even emoji. Every message you send is really a row of these numbers. Challenge: what number would small b be?

faq.a: ASCII is a code table from 1963 that gives each English letter, digit and symbol a number from 0 to 127. Capital A is 65, small a is 97 and the digit 0 is 48.
65 is 64 plus 1, so in 8 bits it is 01000001: the 64s place and the 1s place are on, the rest are off.
Unicode is one huge code table for every writing system in the world, from Devanagari and Chinese to Arabic, Cyrillic and emoji. Its first 128 numbers are the same as ASCII.
asks: How do computers store Hindi or Chinese?

faq.q: How does a computer store letters?
faq.a: It turns each letter into a number using a code table, then stores that number in binary as bits. When it shows the text, it turns the numbers back into letter shapes.
asks: How is text stored in a computer?
Are letters numbers to a computer?

faq.a: Yes. Every emoji has its own Unicode number. The grinning face emoji, for example, is number 128512. Your phone then draws its own picture for that number.

facts: In ASCII and Unicode, capital A is 65 and small a is 97.
ASCII was first published in 1963 and uses 128 codes, 0 to 127.

quiz.say: Capital A is 65. What number is capital C?
quiz.why: Letters are numbered in order: A 65, B 66, C 67.

wrong.1: 66 is B, the letter between A and C.
wrong.2: 99 is small c, not capital C.

quiz.say: Why did the world need Unicode as well as ASCII?

options.show: ASCII had no room for most of the world's writing
options.say: ASCII had no room for most of the world's writing

quiz.why: ASCII has only 128 codes, enough for English but not Hindi, Chinese, Arabic and many more.

wrong.1: Speed was not the problem; the number of characters was.
wrong.2: Computers still store text as numbers; Unicode just has far more of them.
